method: citizen-science camera traps; only independent events kept; hourly activity of squirrels analysed from 1,335 pictures taken at 170 stations (Results 3.2.1)
conditions: Free-ranging urban Eurasian red squirrels, private gardens in Berlin, Germany; camera traps set by volunteers at about 50 cm height with a clear view across the garden, for 4 consecutive weeks in each of five project phases (autumn 2018, spring and autumn 2019, spring and autumn 2020); the first phase was omitted from the analyses; the page does not say whether cameras were baited; the Discussion says many residents installed bird and squirrel feeders during the lockdowns and that 'The additional food sources might have encouraged squirrels to move closer to gardens with feeders.' This record: 1,335 independent squirrel pictures from 170 stations (Results 3.2.1). The same sentence also classes cats (active throughout the day) and martens (primarily crepuscular and nocturnal); this record takes the squirrel clause. The Results also say squirrels were active between 5am and 5pm. The Results give 'collected via 346 stations' for the pictures of all three taxa (1335 squirrel, 14087 cat, 715 marten pictures), and Section 2.3 says '346 out of 516 (67%) stations did not detect any squirrels' (so 170 detected squirrels), so the paper's station counts are not consistent; 170 stations is the figure given for the squirrel hourly analysis ('We used all 1335 pictures of squirrels from 170 stations', Results 3.2.1).
